fields.name: Subject
fields.evidence: InterfaceSystem::ProcessPhotoModePostEventRequests (EoCClient.dll+0xDBD6B0) passes element+0 as ls::Variant<ls::ID<EntityHandleTraits>, ls::TypeWrap<uint64, SoundObjectHandleClassname>> to the ls::GameplaySoundEventRequest constructor (GameEngine export). The variant's 8-byte payload: an entity handle or a sound object id (same idea as SE SoundPostEventRequest.Subject).

fields.name: SubjectType
fields.evidence: Variant alternative index: the writer bg3.exe+0x1E6D710 stores qword 1 at +8 (alternative 1 = sound object handle, the photo-mode sound object at +0); the consumer bg3.exe+0x1F0E360 copies +0..+0xF as one 16-byte variant.

fields.name: Event
fields.evidence: ProcessPhotoModePostEventRequests passes element+0x10 as the FixedString event of the GameplaySoundEventRequest.

fields.name: field_14
fields.evidence: Writer bg3.exe+0x1E6D710 stores 3 (dword); consumer bg3.exe+0x1F0E360 copies it into GameplaySoundEventRequest+0x14 and sets its optional flag at +0x18.

fields.name: Callback
fields.evidence: Writer bg3.exe+0x1E6D710 stores qword 0; the same element type (ecl::sound::PostEventRequest, grown by the same FUN_1406DC490 as the distant-sound requests) holds a pooled ls::SoundCallback pointer here in the dispatcher (Toolkit DispatcherSystem::Update). Not read by the photo-mode consumer.

fields.name: PostEventRequests
fields.evidence: ProcessPhotoModePostEventRequests walks singleton+0 (size +0xC) with stride 0x20 and turns each element into an ls::GameplaySoundEventRequest (stride 0x30) on GameplaySoundEventRequestBusComponent. Writer: ecl::GameplaySoundSystem::Update (macOS name; not found by name in the Toolkit). macOS default zeroes 16 bytes.

open_questions: Meaning of field_14 (always 3 from this writer).
second_pass: Confirmed on Windows: the writer bg3.exe+0x1E6D710 (GameplaySoundSystem, query DAT_1463510EC registered for this singleton by bg3.exe+0x1E6F9A0) appends 0x20-byte elements {qword sound object +0, qword 1 at +8, FixedString +0x10 (e.g. PhotoMode_Exit), dword 3 at +0x14, qword 0 at +0x18}; the consumer bg3.exe+0x1F0E360 walks them with stride 0x20.
